Webhook processor + admin Payment tab contribution

Webhooks & admin operations finish the spine.
Both ride the same event bus.

Webhook processor · extends abstract base
class StripeWebhookProcessor
    extends AbstractWebhookProcessor
{
    protected function verifySignature(
        string $payload, array $headers
    ): bool {
        return $this->adapter->verifyWebhookSignature(
            $payload, $headers['Stripe-Signature'], $this->secret
        );
    }

    protected function routeEvent(WebhookEvent $e): void {
        match ($e->getType()) {
            'payment_intent.succeeded' =>
                $this->dispatcher->dispatch(
                    new PaymentAuthorizedEvent($contract, $ctx)),
            'charge.refunded' =>
                $this->dispatcher->dispatch(
                    new PaymentRefundedEvent($contract, $ctx)),
            // …
        };
    }
}

// Idempotency & logging come from the abstract base.
// Provider-agnostic WebhookLogRepository persists every call.
Capture / Refund services
class StripeCaptureService
    extends AbstractPaymentCaptureService
{
    protected function executeCapture(
        PaymentContractInterface $c, ?float $amount
    ): CaptureResponse {
        return $this->adapter->captureAuthorization(
            new CaptureAuthorizationRequest(
                authorizationId: $c->getProviderOrderId(),
                amount: $amount ? (string) $amount : null,
            )
        );
    }
}
// Partial capture: $amount <= PaymentIntent.amount, irreversible
// Partial refund: total_refunded + amount <= captured
Payment tab · PSP-agnostic, panel-providers contribute

One tab. Every PSP.

Payment Base owns the “Payment” tab on the OXID admin Order Details page (since Sprint I). PSPs do not ship per-PSP admin-order tabs.

Each PSP contributes one or more panel-provider services, tagged oe.payment.admin_panel. Payment Base’s tab collects them via !tagged_iterator.

# stripe/services.yaml
StripeOrderRefundPanelProvider:
    tags:
      - { name: oe.payment.admin_panel,
          provider: stripe, priority: 100 }

# Order Refund flow uses shared admin services
OrderRefundViewDataProvider:    # cached PI/charge fetch
    arguments: ['@stripe.adapter']
OrderActionDispatcher:          # dispatches capture/refund events
    arguments: ['@event.dispatcher']
Admin operations ride the same events
  • Admin clicks “Capture” → OrderActionDispatcher dispatches StripeCaptureRequestEvent
  • StripeCaptureRequestHandler (priority 0) executes via the adapter
  • oe_payments_transaction records the audit trail; OXPAID updated by OrderPaymentCompletedHandler
  • Self-healing on view: reconcilePaymentState() repairs OXPAID if Stripe Dashboard bypassed the webhook chain
The whole spine is reusable. A second PSP — PayPal — ships exactly the same shape: adapter + 4 events + 6 handlers + webhook processor + 1 panel provider. Stripe and PayPal are peers: neither imports the other; both share Payment Base.
